title: compact-on-access-reclaimer-and-bandwidth-aware-spill-policy
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Introduce compact-on-access KV reclaimer and a bandwidth-aware spill controller to reduce memory fragmentation and smooth spill traffic under tenant hotspots. Improves memory efficiency and reduces tail latency during eviction-driven workloads.
description:
Motivation: Production workloads with skewed tenant access patterns were triggering frequent full-segment compactions and heavy spill bursts that increased tail latency and egress IO costs. Existing eviction policies prioritized recency/size without accounting for fragmentation or downstream spill bandwidth. This change implements a compact-on-access reclaimer that opportunistically coalesces fragmented slots during normal access paths and a bandwidth-aware spill policy that rate-limits spills per-host and per-tenant to avoid I/O storming.

Summary of changes: Added a lightweight in-path compaction pass that runs when a page/slot is touched and fragmentation crosses a tenant-specific threshold; introduced a composite eviction score combining recency, fragmentation-penalty, and host-io-cost; implemented a SpillController that monitors host egress bandwidth and enforces tenant spill windows and backpressure signals; extended kernel_selector to prefer compact-friendly kernels when compact-on-access is enabled; added observability for fragmentation_score, spill_budget, and spill_backpressure events.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2147)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] End-to-end perf benchmarked on benchmark-lab infra
- [x] Migration strategy for existing caches (toggle via runtime flag)
- [x] Metrics + dashboard tiles created in observability-pack

Design notes: The compact-on-access reclaimer is intentionally conservative: it attempts small coalesces limited to the current page neighborhood to avoid long pauses. It uses a lightweight fragmentation estimator (slot occupancy run-length analysis) to decide when to run. The eviction score is computed as: base_lru_score + alpha * fragmentation_penalty + beta * host_io_cost, where alpha/beta are runtime-tunable. The SpillController exposes soft and hard budgets: soft budgets throttle spills with delayed scheduling, hard budgets defer non-critical writebacks and escalate to tenant rate-limiters. To avoid cross-tenant interference, the controller tracks per-tenant recent spill bytes and enforces a fairness window.

Compatibility & rollout: Feature guarded behind runtime flag: runtime.kv.compact_on_access and runtime.kv.bandwidth_spill_controller. Default: disabled. We plan a staged rollout: opt-in on dedicated sandboxes, then enable with conservative alpha/beta on canary fleet, and finally enable on main with telemetry gating. Migration does not require on-disk changes.

Testing & perf: Benchmarks on benchmark-lab using a synthetic hotspot workload (90% of accesses to 8% of keys) show: median token-serve latency change: +1% (noise); 95th percentile latency: -9% to -14% depending on alpha; host spill egress bytes: -32% peak; resident fragmentation_score (aggregate): -18% after 30 minutes of steady state. Memory overhead: +0.8% for the compact-on-access metadata.

Files touched (high-level): kv/cache/reclaimer.cc, kv/cache/reclaimer.h, kv/evictor/score_calculator.cc, scheduler/spill_controller.go, runtime/kernel_selector.cc, runtime/config/runtime_flags.proto, tools/benchmark-lab/hotspot-sweep.yaml, observability/metrics/kv_fragmentation.prom, tests/kv/reclaimer_test.cc, tests/kv/spill_controller_integration.cc, docs/design/compact_on_access.md.

Operational considerations: SpillController emits backpressure events that are surfaced as a new alert (KVSpillBackpressureHigh) with severity P2. Owners can tune soft_budget_ms and tenant_window_bytes. We added dashboards for tenant spill windows, host egress utilization, and fragmentation heatmaps.

Related work: complements earlier eviction work (ENG-3378) by adding IO-budget awareness and in-path coalescing. This avoids the aggressive async compactions we observed in pr-xxxxxx patterns that caused large background IO spikes.

Implementation notes: The reclaimer integrates with existing KV lock-free structures; compaction operates on per-page runs and yields after a configurable cycle budget to prevent head-of-line blocking. The SpillController is implemented in Go in the scheduler plane and communicates via the placement RPC to runtime nodes to apply spill pacing tokens. Kernel selector was extended to set a compact-friendly kernel flag when the runtime option is enabled.

Rollout timeline: Feature branch created 2025-11-03. Initial prototype in integration tests 2025-12. Benchmarks and safety tests 2026-01. This PR finalizes the implementation and wiring for canary rollout (2026-02).

Why this is different: Prior PRs focused on large background compaction and eviction heuristics; this PR targets low-latency, incremental coalescing at access time and explicit spill budget control to smooth I/O without sacrificing tail latency.

review_thread:
Evan Wu: Can the compaction pass hold for long periods under pathological access patterns? Suggest adding a max_cycle_budget.
Priya Desai: Added cycle_budget with a default of 5ms and conservative defaults in runtime flags.

Marcus O'Neill: SpillController looks solid but we need a migration story for clusters without egress meters.
Priya Desai: Controller falls back to token-count heuristics when egress meters are unavailable; documented in design doc.

Sofia Klein: Please add more telemetry for per-tenant fairness and ensure we don't starve low-throughput tenants.
Priya Desai: Added tenant_window_bytes and fairness_ratio metric; integration tests simulate low-throughput tenants to verify no starvation.
